evidence.hard_stops_checked: Checked and clear: no pricing or offer change, no factual business claim, no user-visible copy added or changed, no secrets or credentials touched, no deployment performed, no third-party service added, no external outreach, no PII. No URL added or removed — this only links pages that already exist.
evidence.reviewer_ensemble: builder pass, skeptic pass, taste pass — see the reviewer_ensemble object.
evidence.reviewer_disagreement_reviewed: The skeptic's objection was that automated cross-language slug matching is exactly the kind of fuzzy step that ships wrong hreflang, and wrong hreflang is worse than none because a non-equivalent pair can invalidate the whole cluster. Accepted rather than argued down, and answered with three concrete guards: 1:1 assignment instead of best-match (which caught real collisions — two English event pages and two drone pages each claiming the same Spanish page), an explicit exclusion of the one geographically loose pair (west-palm-beach vs palm-beach-county), and a route-existence assertion over all 184 emitted targets.
evidence.winner_rationale: Pairing existing pages is the highest-value change available that adds no URLs: it gives bilingual readers a real toggle, tells Google the two language versions are the same page rather than competing duplicates, and consolidates signal on a site whose problem is 259 URLs earning 63 impressions. Building new English area hubs would serve the same directive but requires authored marketing copy, so it was deliberately left out of an automated change.
evidence.tests_or_validation: pnpm check green end to end: lint, typecheck, 227/227 tests across 39 files, production build. CHECK_EXIT=0. Separately, a script asserted every one of the 184 hreflang targets resolves to a real page.tsx route (0 missing).

builder.evidence: 36 pairs (72 entries) appended to languageAlternates in lib/spanish-site.ts. The 17 pre-existing shell pairs are untouched. Consumers are unchanged: lib/site-metadata.ts already reads languageAlternates for alternates.languages, and app/sitemap.ts already emits alternates from the same map, so both metadata and sitemap pick the pairs up with no code change.

skeptic.evidence: The matching was not trusted on score alone. Greedy 1:1 assignment surfaced and fixed two genuine collisions (event vs nightlife-event; drone-video-editing vs real-estate-drone-video-editing) that a best-match pass had gotten wrong. One pair was excluded outright as non-equivalent content. All 184 emitted targets were checked against the real route set with zero missing. x-default=English is grounded in measured data, not preference: Semrush returns no US volume for the Spanish Miami terms.

taste.evidence: A block comment records why the pairs exist, why x-default is English, and what the state was before, so a future reader does not mistake the map for autogenerated noise or flip x-default without the search evidence.

reviewer_disagreement_reviewed: Skeptic held that fuzzy cross-language matching risks shipping wrong hreflang. Answered with 1:1 assignment, an explicit exclusion, and a 184-target route-existence check rather than by asserting the matcher was good.
winner_rationale: Link the pages that already exist before building new ones — no URL growth on a site already carrying 259 URLs for 63 impressions.
